tagline: Oak-shaded roads to the towns that moved out for the rockets.
intro: Four-lane Highway 607 runs north to the gates of Stennis Space Center, where the first and second stages of the Saturn V were test-fired, and five more roads make up the rest of the network through the 125,000-acre acoustic buffer zone around it. They run through pine plantation and hardwoods, often under oaks.

The other five are named for Pearlington, at the zone's edge, and for the towns that had to go when the zone was drawn, Logtown, Napoleon, Westonia and Santa Rosa. No habitable building may go up in the zone without a special exception, which, the byway plan noted, suited the beekeepers who kept hives among the pines with no neighbors to mind them.

moments.title: Logtown
moments.text: The H. Weston Lumber Company once kept over 3,000 people here, and now three family cemeteries, some old foundations and an artesian well by the Pearl River are what remain.

moments.title: Turtle Skin Cemetery
moments.text: Inside a stuccoed block wall on the site of the old Corinth Baptist Church, graves going back to the 1860s still say that Santa Rosa was here.

sources.label: MDOT, Byways to Space Scenic Byway Corridor Management Plan
